doc.title: Frank Foster interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 7, 1998

title: Big band records introduced by his older brother
summary: His brother introduced him to Basie, Lunceford and Ellington, and he zeroed in on Basie.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: What was your first exposure to music of the big band era. Was it through records and/or radio?

Through recordings and especially introduced to me by my older brother. I had a brother who was six years my senior. So when I was eight he was fourteen. And he had me listen to bands from eight years old on, and he was seventeen I guess I was however, six years younger. And he had me listen especially to Count Basie, Jimmie Lunceford and Duke Ellington. And I zeroed in on those three, most particularly on Count Basie. And I just became a big band nut.
